name: IPIP-VIA-R
items_note: Items copied from https://ipip.ori.org/IPIP-VIA-R_Key.html, 3 November 2026. The key page lists items by scale without an administration order; the items here are interleaved across the scales in round-robin order. The key page prints "Weigh the pro's and the con's ." with a space before the full stop; that space is dropped. Scale names on the site are the short forms of the published names, which are kept in publishedName.

source.paper: Bluemke, M., Partsch, M. V., Saucier, G., & Lechner, C. M. (2021). Measuring cross-cultural supermodel strengths in a balanced way: The IPIP-VIA-R short scales. Assessment (as cited on the IPIP key page)

licence.text: Public domain (IPIP). Permission is granted automatically for any person to use IPIP items for any purpose, commercial or non-commercial.

instructions: Describe yourself as you generally are now, not as you wish to be in the future. Describe yourself as you honestly see yourself, in relation to other people you know of the same sex as you are, and roughly your same age.

items.text: Feel it's important to live in a world of beauty.
Know that there are people in my life who care as much for me as for themselves.
Am an extremely loyal person.
Am excited by many different activities.
Treat all people equally.
Try to respond with understanding when someone treats me badly.
Express my thanks to those who care about me.
Can find the positive in what seems negative to others.

reliabilitySource: Coefficient alpha per scale for the UK sample (n = 474) from the IPIP key page, which gives Germany/UK figures for alpha, McDonald's omega and two-to-three-week test-retest reliability. The authors say alpha understates the reliability of these balanced four-item scales and recommend omega.
